Alqama

English

03

“Whoever thinks that God will never help him in this world and the…”

An explanation transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās (Q 22:15).

663
Explanation from Ibn ʿAbbās No. 663: 3: 6

Ibn ʿAbbās

English
Transmission wording
663: 3:6. Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, on His words
"Whoever thinks that God will never help him in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the sky": He said, whoever thinks that God will not help Muhammad, peace be upon him, let him extend a rope to the ceiling of his house and strangle himself with it (verse 15).
العربية
663: 3: 6 سفيان عن أبي إسحق عن التميمي عن بن عباس في قوله كان ظن أَنْ لَنْ يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى السماء قَالَ مَنْ كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَنْ لن ينصر الله محمدا ص = فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِحَبْلٍ فِي سَمَاءِ بَيْتِهِ فليختنق به (الآية 15) .

04

“These are two adversaries who disputed about their Lord”

An explanation transmitted from Qays ibn Abbad (Q 22:19).

664
Explanation from Qays ibn Abbad No. 664: 4: 5

Qays ibn Abbad

English
Transmission wording
664: 4:5. Sufyan, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn Abbad, who said:
I heard Abu Dharr swear by God that this verse was revealed concerning six of Quraysh: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ubayda ibn al-Harith, Utba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabia, and al-Walid ibn Utba: "These are two adversaries who disputed about their Lord," to the end of the verse (verse 19).
العربية
664: 4: 5 سفيان عن أبي هاشم عن أبي مِجْلَزٍ عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ يُقْسِمُ بِاللَّهِ لَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ فِي سِتَّةٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ حَمْزَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ وَعَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طالب وعبيدة بن الحرث وَعُتْبَةَ وَشَيْبَةَ ابْنَا رَبِيعَةَ وَالْوَلِيدِ ابن عتبة هذان خاصمان عن اختصموا في ربهم الى آخر الأية (الآية 19) .
Edition record 371448 · p. 209Link to report ↗
05

“You are an akif [one who stays]”

Two explanations transmitted from Abu Husayn and Ibn Masʿūd (Q 22:25).

665
Explanation from Abu Husayn No. 665: 5: 18

Abu Husayn

English
Transmission wording
665: 5:18. Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, who said:
I wanted to perform itikaf, so I asked Said ibn Jubayr, and he said, "You are an akif [one who stays]." Then he recited "equal are the resident therein and the visitor" (verse 25).
العربية
665: 5: 18 سفيان عَنْ أَبِي حُصَيْنٍ قَالَ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَعْتَكِفَ فَقُلْتُ سَأَلْتُ سَعِيدَ بْنَ جُبَيْرٍ قَالَ أَنْتَ عَاكِفٌ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ سَوَاءً الْعَاكِفُ فِيهِ والباد (الآية 25) .
Edition record 371448 · p. 209Link to report ↗
666
Explanation from Ibn Masʿūd No. 666: 6: 19

Ibn Masʿūd

English
Transmission wording
666: 6:19. Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from Ibn Masud, that he said: Whoever intends a sin and does not commit it, it is not recorded against him until he commits it. But if a man intended, while saying he would kill a man at the House [of God], God would make him taste a painful punishment. Then he recited
"and whoever intends therein ⦗p. 210⦘ deviation by wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment" (verse 25).
العربية

Edition record 371449 · p. 210Link to report ↗
671
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 671: 11: 1

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
671: 11:1. Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said:
Abraham, peace be upon him, was commanded to proclaim the pilgrimage, so he stood on the Station and it grew with him until it became like the tallest mountain. He called out, "O people, answer your Lord," twice. They answered him from beneath the seven seas: "Here we are, we have answered. Here we are, we have obeyed." So whoever performs the pilgrimage until the Day of Resurrection is one who ⦗p. 211⦘ answered him. It settled in the heart of every Muslim (verse 27).
العربية
671: 11: 1 سفيان عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ قَالَ أُمِرَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ﷺ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ بِالْحَجِّ فَقَامَ عَلَى الْمَقَامِ فَتَطَاوَلَ بِهِ حَتَّى صَارَ كَأَطْوَلِ جَبَلٍ فَنَادَى يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَجِيُبوا رَبَّكُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ فَأَجَابُوهُ مِنْ تَحْتِ الْبُحُورِ السَّبْعِ لَبَّيْكَ أَجَبْنَا لَبَّيْكَ أَطَعْنَا فَمَنْ حَجَّ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَهُوَ مَنِ ⦗p. 211⦘ اسْتَجَابَ لَهُ فَوَقَرَتْ فِي نفس كل مسلم (الآية 27) .
